response: The format "#;#;0;General" in Excel is a custom number format that applies different display rules based on the value of the cell. It consists of four parts separated by semicolons. The first part applies to positive numbers, the second to negative numbers, the third to zero, and the fourth to any other value. In this case, positive and negative numbers will be displayed as is, zero will be displayed as 0, and any other value will use the General format.
